subject: ventures/photo-editing
professional: a working event/wedding photographer who also edits video (culls 2,000 frames after a shoot, grades with LUTs, cuts reels); first checks: is the sharp-at-100% pick right and are deliberate low-key/high-key frames spared, is the tilt reading right, is ingest verified and non-destructive, does the public page tell the truth about what runs

evidence.correctness: Third audit; numpy, scipy and OpenCV are not installed in this sandbox, so references are pure-Python re-implementations and ffmpeg, none written by the author. Script run: python3 chk.py (scratchpad). (a) shootflow.frame_analysis._laplacian_variance vs statistics.pvariance of an independently built 4-neighbour Laplacian list: noise frame 719.210320772637 = 719.210320772637, checker 5150.392198431206 = 5150.392198431206, ramp 0.39936118033305645 = 0.39936118033305645 (exact). (b) noise_sigma_from_frame on Gaussian-noise frames of measured std 3.019 and 7.989: tool 2.965 and 7.907; independent Immerkaer mean-abs formula 2.999 and 7.947. Within 2% of truth. (c) _luma_stats mean 120.0 on a 40/200 checker = ffmpeg signalstats YAVG=120; exposure 1.0 matches the documented formula by hand. (d) tilt_from_frame on synthetic soft horizons of true tilt 0, +3, -4 degrees read 0.0, 2.993, -3.991 (confidence 1.0). (e) dhash_hex vs a reference that uses ffmpeg `scale=9:8:flags=area` then the same left>right compare, on a sinusoid+noise frame: tool d24b2da5965a4b2d, ffmpeg-based d24b2da4965a492d: 3 of 64 bits differ (ffmpeg rounds cells to 8-bit and uses fractional cell weights, the tool floors the 320/9 cell edges). That is a real but small difference, well inside a burst-grouping threshold, and I cannot call it a bug. All frames synthetic; no real camera RAW available, so correctness stays capped at 3.
evidence.completeness: README claims re-checked against the same tree: git log shows the only commit touching ventures/photo-editing since the r2 audit is unrelated (clothing-design-studio PDF), so the code and page are byte-identical to r2. Cull, frame metrics (sharpness, exposure, noise, tilt, framing, dHash) all ran above and worked. Not re-run this round: checksummed ingest, local pipeline/LUT grade, reels (ran in the 2026-11-07 round, code unchanged). Stated gaps stand: RAW development, no app, look/scene stages are stand-ins, no console-script install. No NotImplementedError found. 3 against its own README, as a CLI.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/photo-editing && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: Ran 517 tests in ~22 s, FAILED (failures=1, errors=1, skipped=1). Failure: test_workspace_health.test_unreadable_render_input_is_reported_for_review (chmod(0) is no barrier as root; line 117); error: test_real_photo_calibration.test_tilt_crop_removes_corners_and_keeps_aspect (PIL._imaging ImportError in this sandbox, no importorskip). Both identical to r2 and unfixed. Three seeded mutations in frame_analysis.py, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards): M1 exposure target `abs(mean - 120.0)` -> 100.0: NOT caught (suite result identical to baseline, 1 failure 1 error); M2 _SHARPNESS_HALF_POINT 60 -> 30: CAUGHT (failures rose 1 to 2); M3 dHash comparison `>` -> `>=`: NOT caught. 1 of 3 caught. The exposure-target gap has now survived three audits (r1 M1, r2 M1, r3 M1). 2.
evidence.craft: Read frame_analysis.py (metrics_from_frames, noise_sigma_from_frame, dhash_hex, _laplacian_variance, _luma_stats, story_score). Formulas documented with derivation (Immerkaer) and named constants. Defects: per-pixel pure-Python loops, with a full sort of 57k responses for the median, and no vectorised path; magic blend weights (0.6/0.4, 0.85/0.15, 0.5/0.3/0.2) not calibrated; exposure grey 120 and the 2*(shadows+highlights) penalty are inline literals not named constants (and unpinned by tests); dHash floors cell edges so it differs from a standard area-scaled dHash by a few bits; parallel dry-run adapter/scheduler stack beside the real ffmpeg path; 18 modules, several of thousands of lines. Not re-run this round: ruff (r2 recorded 69 errors). 2.
evidence.claims: Loaded and read ventures/photo-editing/site/index.html lines 30-52: unchanged from r1 and r2. 'What does not exist yet' says 'The renderers are dry-run placeholders: ShootFlow does not yet render video or grade images'; the FAQ repeats 'No. The renderers are dry-run placeholders'. Both contradict the pipeline's real ffmpeg render/grade path (demonstrated r1). Lines 34 and 47 tell users to run `shootflow cull FOLDER --out REPORT`; grep of pyproject.toml shows no [project.scripts] entry, so the command is not installed (working form: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m shootflow.cli cull). Honest parts: the page says cull has not been measured on a real shoot, keeps the no-upload statement and the 'early-stage' backup warning. The cull claims are backed by the code that ran this round. Two audits' worth of notice and still no fix, so no higher than 2.
evidence.fitness: Job: cull a shoot folder, get a ranked XMP-tagged selection. It runs in one command offline with sidecars and no upload (verified r2, code unchanged). Still no install, no UI, RAW only through the embedded preview, reels silent, and never validated against a human's picks on a real shoot (VENTURE.yaml stage prototype). A photographer could try it as a first pass; they could not rely on it. 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with Photo Mechanic/Lightroom culling practice (focus checked at 100% on eyes, one keeper per burst, deliberate low-key frames kept) and standard image-quality methods. Sound: sha256 ingest, XMP star semantics, dHash burst grouping, Immerkaer noise, structure-tensor tilt with undo of non-uniform stretch (reproduced above). Departures: analysis on a 320x180 downscale hides critical-focus misses; exposure is distance of mean luma from grey 120 with clipping penalty, so low-key and high-key frames score badly; eyes-open off by default; weights uncalibrated against any human cull. Useful first pass, not a sign-off. 2.

defects.what: Public product page still says the renderers are dry-run placeholders and that ShootFlow does not render video or grade images (false), and tells users to run a `shootflow` command that pyproject.toml does not install. Unchanged across three audits.
Exposure scoring is unpinned: changing the grey target 120 to 100 leaves the entire 517-test suite result unchanged (third audit in a row). The dHash comparison operator is also unpinned.
Sharpness, exposure and tilt are read from a 320x180 gray downscale, so critical-focus misses are invisible and deliberate low-key/high-key frames are penalised.
Two tests fail in a root/minimal sandbox without a guard (chmod(0) as root; Pillow-dependent test with no importorskip). Fix is a skipIf(os.geteuid()==0) and a pytest/unittest import guard.

dHash floors the 320/9 cell edges, so 3 of 64 bits differ from an area-scaled reference; harmless for burst grouping but not the standard algorithm. Pure-Python pixel loops and a duplicated dry-run engine remain.

verdict: Third audit in three days with no change to the venture between r2 and r3, so scores are unchanged: correctness 3 and completeness 3 (the numeric core reproduces exactly against independent Laplacian, within 2% on noise, exactly on luma versus ffmpeg, within 0.01 degrees on tilt, and 3 bits off a standard dHash), verification 2 (1 of 3 seeded mutations caught; the exposure target is still unpinned), craft, claims, fitness and domain 2. It does not meet the bar because the public page's false 'does not render or grade' statement and uninstalled command have survived three audits, and because verification is under 3. The cheapest route to the bar is a three-line page edit plus one exposure test.
